Between dates stated above, detectives detailed
for investigation into this crime, have continued
their enquiries, and although information has been
obtained to the effect that this assassination was
instigated by the occupants of 35 Edinburgh Road,
yet no definite proof in support of this information
is forthcoming.

According to the information received, it
would appear that the late Det. Inspt. had for some
time prior to his death been harassing these people
through his repeated investigations into their
activities and that although they had tried to
approach him with the promise of a monthly subsidy
he had refused to accept same. This refusal apparent-
ly raised the ire of the officer i/c of "35" and it was
at his instigation the assassination was carried out.

As already mentioned nothing in the way of defini-
te proof has been obtained to support this information,
hence until such time as this proof can be obtained,
this case is respectfully submitted for classification.

1940年7月15日

在上述日期之间，被指派调查此罪案的侦探继续进行了查询，虽然已获得情报称此次暗杀系由爱丁堡路35号的居住者所唆使，但尚无确凿证据支持该情报。

根据所获情报，已故督察在生前一段时间内，因反复调查这些人的活动而对他们进行骚扰，尽管他们曾试图以承诺每月提供津贴的方式接近他，但他拒绝接受。这一拒绝显然激怒了“35号”负责人的怒火，暗杀行动即是在其唆使下实施的。

如前所述，目前尚未获得任何确凿证据来支持这一情报，因此，在获得此类证据之前，谨将此案提交归档分类。

On the morning of 28-4-40 an inquest was
held on the body of the late Det. Inspr. Loh Kung Sung
(陸根生) at the General Undertakers, Changping Road,
and after all evidence had been heard the following
verdict was handed down by Procurator Deng Pei Yuan
(唐沛元) :-

" Death due to bullet wounds, body to be
removed by deceased's brother Det. Sgt.
Loh Kung Dee (陸根弟) for burial. "

The personal property of deceased was
returned to his brother on the 28-4-40.

With reference to the .32 Automatic Browning
pistol No. 17694, used in the assassination of the
deceased and subsequently seized by the Police at the
scene of the crime, same on being examined by the
Arms Identification Section was found to have the
following past history :-

It would appear that in September 1939, this
pistol which then bore makers No. "Y61", was licensed
by the Shanghai Municipal Police in the name of Mr.
Yu Hung Lung (俞鴻鈞), then Councillor to the
Municipality of Greater Shanghai and that in December
1939, this licence number Y. 2964 was cancelled, the
pistol being retained by the licensee.

1940年4月28日上午，在昌平路通用殡仪馆对已故督察陆根生（Loh Kung Sung）的遗体举行了死因研讯，在听取所有证词后，检察官邓沛元（Procurator Deng Pei Yuan，原文注：唐沛元）作出了如下裁决：

“死于枪伤，遗体由其弟、警佐陆根弟（Loh Kung Dee）领回安葬。”

死者的个人财产已于1940年4月28日归还其弟。

关于用于暗杀死者、随后被警方在犯罪现场缴获的勃朗宁.32口径自动手枪（编号17694），经枪械识别科检验，发现其具有以下既往历史：

看来在1939年9月，这支当时标有制造商编号“Y61”的手枪，以时任大上海市政府参事俞鸿钧（Yu Hung Lung）的名义在上海公共租界工部局警务处登记注册；而在1939年12月，该执照号码 Y. 2964 被注销，手枪由持照人保留。

On the 15-2-36, in the course of rounding up
a gang of "Armed Robbers", detectives attached to
Hongkew Station raided a straw hut off Hang Feong
Road, Chapel, and amongst other things seized an empty
cartridge case and bullet, which on examination was
found to have been fired from above mentioned pistol,
however the weapon in question was never found (See
Hongkew Misc. 112/36). Investigation into this angle
of the case will be made the subject of a further diary.

As previously mentioned this pistol, on being
presented for licensing in September 1939, bore makers
No. "762" and later S.M. Police No. Y. 2004, however
on being seized on the 27-4-40, the former number was
found to have been altered to "17624" by adding the
1 and 4 at either end, whilst the latter number was
found to have been erased.

The last occasion on which this pistol came
to the notice of the S.M. Police was on the 27th

S.H. Police, was interviewed on the afternoon of

was one and the same pistol (Statement attached).

In view of these disclosures the above mentioned
prisoner was further questioned as to why this pistol
had not been seized at the time of arrest by the
British Military and he, in replying, stated that in
all probability same was then being kept at 35 Edinburgh
Road, from which address all pistols were then issued.

According to the list in question, this
particular pistol was issued to one named Chiang Vung
Iang (蒋凤林), who was arrested along with the
prisoner already mentioned, but, who unfortunately
has already been disposed of, hence no further
corroboration can be had from him.

The aforegoing facts more or less definitely
establish from which source the pistol used in this
crime originated, however up to the present it is
still too premature to voice any definite opinion re
the motive for the assassination of deceased and with
this end in view enquiries are now being continued.

1940年4月30日下午接受了问询，结果他证实了这确实是同一支手枪（陈述书附后）。

鉴于这些披露，上述囚犯被进一步讯问，为何这支手枪在英军逮捕时未被缴获，他回答说，很可能当时它被存放在爱丁堡路35号，所有手枪都是从该地址发出的。

根据相关清单，这支特定手枪是发给一名叫蒋凤林（Chiang Vung Iang）的人的，他与前述囚犯一同被捕，但不幸的是，此人已被处置（原文意指已死亡或被秘密处理），因此无法从他那里获得进一步的佐证。

上述事实或多或少地确定了用于此罪案的手枪的来源，然而截至目前，就死者被暗杀的动机发表任何确切意见还为时过早，为此，查询工作仍在继续。

〔签名〕

Date April 29, 1940.
Subject Murder of D.I. LOH KENG SUNG
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

In connection with the murder of D.I. LOH
KENG SUNG of the Municipal Police, which took place
on Chengtu Road on April 27, information has been
received to the effect that the assassination was
perpetrated by the "Youth Group" ( 青年團 ),
a branch of the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army located at House 119, Lane 37,
Brenan Road (near Jessfield Park). The deceased
officer is alleged to have secured information and
supplied same to the Municipal Police, on the
activities of the pro-Wang Ching Wei organizations
which was obtained through a number of his followers
frequenting the Zao Ka Doo District and employed
by the Corps at 76 Jessfield Road.

It is stated by the same informant that
a watch has been maintained on the movements of
the late D.I. LOH KENG SUNG for several months,
and an attempt on two occasions in December, 1939
was made on his life, but failed because of
precautions taken by the deceased himself.

C. Crawford
D. I.
D.C. (Special Branch).

D.I. Loh when questioned in hospital prior to his death was unable to speak, and in answer to questions indicated that there was only one man responsible for the crime and that he did not recognise him.

Police in the vicinity located several witnesses of the crime, they were brought to the Station and statements taken (attached). All these witnesses state that after the first shot was fired their attention was attracted and they observed the male Chinese in foreign dress shoot D.I. Loh in the back and then after discarding the pistol, run into alleyway 33 Chengtu Road, this alleyway has another entrance, Lane 411 Taku Road, and it was probably by this alleyway that the assassin made good his escape. Immediately after the crime detectives made enquiries at all houses in this alley-way but none of the occupants could give any information to Police.

In an effort to discover some motive for the crime and the murderer, the effects of D.I. Loh were searched, on his person was found 2-$10 notes, 8-$5 notes, 30-$1 notes, small money amounting to $1.42, on Sincere Co. cheque for $10, 2 Japanese military notes for 50 sen and 10 sen, also a number of personal papers. | |

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of S.P.I. 1976 Woo Hai Tung.
native of ........................................ taken by me himself.
at No. Rd. Stn. on the 27 '4/40. translated and interpreted by Interpreter [此处转录不清].

S.P.I. 1976 Woo Hai Tung states as follows :-

On the 27/4/40 I was on 2nd day duty and was detailed to patrol No. 4 beat section, from 3 - 7 p.m. At about 5.40 p.m. while I was at the entrance to the Tzuyunyah near Toku Road, I suddenly heard 4 pistol shots. I immediately rushed to the spot upon my arrival. I observed a male Chinese lying on the pavement outside No. 62 Mengtu Road. I was informed by a person at the scene that the assassin had escaped into Lane 33 Mengtu Road, so I immediately blew my police whistle and simultaneously ran into Lane No. 33 in order to chase him, but I could not find him, he having already disappeared prior to my entering into the lane. I then returned to the scene and reported the case to the station by telephone. Following this, I made a search in the vicinity which resulted in a pistol loaded with one round of ammunition being found abandoned at a place about 15 yards away from Lane 46 Chengtu Road, and in addition I also picked up a letter which was lying at a place about 15 yards away from the place where the pistol was found.

When I was blowing the whistle, S.P.I. 187 who was on traffic duty at the intersection of Chengtu Road and Ave. Roch, rushed to the scene, and following his arrival, I then went to ring up station by street telephone No. 7. A few moments later a party of detectives arrived and S.M.P. ambulance attended in which the injured person was removed to the Police Hospital for treatment.

Signed.

特别巡捕 1976 号吴海通陈述如下：-

1940年4月27日，我处于第二天当值状态，被派往第4巡逻段执行下午3时至7时的巡逻任务。下午约5时40分，当我位于德都路（Toku Road）附近的慈云雅（Tzuyunyah）入口处时，突然听到四声枪响。我立即赶赴现场。抵达后，我看见一名华籍男子躺在孟脱路（Mengtu Road）62号外的人行道上。现场有人告知我刺客已逃入孟脱路33弄，于是我立即吹响警笛，同时跑进33弄试图追捕，但未能找到他，因为他在我进入弄堂之前已经消失。随后我返回现场，并通过电话向巡捕房报案。此后，我在附近进行搜索，结果在成都路（Chengtu Road）46弄约15码远处发现一支装有一发子弹的手枪被遗弃在该处，此外，我还捡到一封信，该信位于发现手枪处约15码远的地方。

当我吹哨时，正在成都路与福煦路（Ave. Roch，即福煦路）交叉口执行交通任务的特别巡捕 187 号赶至现场，在他到达后，我便去使用7号街头电话亭致电巡捕房。几分钟后，一队侦探赶到，工部局救护车也随即到达，伤者被送往警察医院接受治疗。

签名。

India                                      D.J. Snuggs.
Ch. Rd. Stn.          27-4-40              self.

My name is Vernail Singh son of Rauta Singh Village Sursin
Post Office Ramsingh District Lahore. I am attached to Chengtu
Road Police Station.

On the afternoon of 27-4-40, I was detailed for traffic
post duty at the corner of Avenue Foch and Chengtu Road (Post
No. 4) between the hours of 4 p.m. and 8 p.m.

At about 5.30 p.m. whilst I was on duty, I heard the report
of pistol shots being fired, my attention was immediately attracted
by these reports which sounded as though they had been fired
at point on Chengtu Road near Taku Road. I immediately left my
post and proceeded running in a Northerly direction along Cheng-
tu Road in order to enquire. After running about 50 yards I
observed a male Chinese dressed in a dark coloured foreign style
suit running towards me, the latter was carrying a pistol in
his right hand and was approximately 20 yards away from me, on
the same side of the road as I was on (East).

The male Chinese who apparently also noticed me proceeding
towards him, immediately discarded his pistol and turned into an
alleyway. I made my way, direct to the discarded pistol where
I was met by C.P.C. 1276 who picked up same. This C.P.C. and I
then proceeded together to the corner of Avenue Foch and Chengtu
Road where the C.P.C. telephoned the station from St. telephone
box No. 7 reporting the matter.

The above is my true statement.

Signed:-
S.P.C. 127.

特别巡捕 127 号 卡纳尔·辛格（Karnail Singh）。
印度                                      D.J. Snuggs。
成都路巡捕房          1940年4月27日              本人。

我叫弗纳尔·辛格（Vernail Singh），是劳塔·辛格（Rauta Singh）之子，来自拉合尔区（Lahore District）拉姆辛格邮局（Post Office Ramsingh）苏尔辛村（Village Sursin）。我隶属于成都路巡捕房。

1940年4月27日下午，我被派往福煦路（Avenue Foch）与成都路交叉口的交通岗（第4号岗）执勤，时间为下午4时至8时。

下午约5时30分，当我正在执勤时，听到手枪射击声，这些声音立刻引起了我的注意，听起来像是在成都路靠近大沽路（Taku Road）附近某点发射的。我立即离开岗位，沿成都路向北奔跑以查问情况。跑了约50码后，我看见一名身穿深色西式服装的华籍男子向我跑来，后者右手持有一支手枪，距离我约20码，与我同在道路的同一侧（东侧）。

这名华籍男子显然也注意到我正向他走去，他立即丢弃手枪并转入一条小巷。我径直走向那支被丢弃的手枪，在那里遇到了华籍警长 1276 号（C.P.C. 1276），他捡起了手枪。随后我与该名华籍警长一同前往福煦路与成都路的交叉口，该华籍警长从7号街头电话亭致电巡捕房报告此事。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：-
特别巡捕 127 号。

Yang Yung Piau, age 48, native of Ningpo, proprietor of the

At about 5 p.m. 27/4/40, when I was talking business

wearing black foreign dress, age about 40, height about 5'5",
medium build, dark round face, fire about 3 or 4 shots from

turned round his head and looked at his assassin, whilst the
latter immediately escaped towards south and disappeared. At
this moment, the injured person was staggering, waving his hand
in order to get a ricksha, but all the ricksha coolies in that
vicinity refused to approach him. Following this he collapsed
onto the ground.

At about 5.30 p.m. 27 4/40, whilst I was sitting in the

roadway and observed a person of strong build, staggering on
the pavement opposite my shop. He raised his hand in order to

observed him discard his pistol at a place about 15 yards
away from the scene, and insert his left hand into his jacket
pocket from which he took out a letter and threw onto the
roadway. Following this, he continued to walk south but later
ran into Lane No. 37 Chengtu Road upon seeing the approach of
Sgt. **〔此处转录不清〕**, who was on traffic duty at the intersection of
